flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the Italian bishop. It points at f7, which is why this opening exists, and you gave me a blank 'strongest move' with a development tag you didn't even say out loud. If you're going to name-drop the Anti-Fried Liver two plies later in the metadata, teach me that this bishop is the piece Ng5 would team up with.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: h6 is the Anti-Fried Liver: it stops Ng5 hitting f7. You classified it best, then taught me nothing. A 1200 playing this on purpose wants to hear 'this keeps the knight off g5,' not a shrug and 'That's the one.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the black pawn.
flags.critique: d4 is the central break: you crack e5 while Black's king is still in the middle. You instead sold a discovered attack from c1 onto h6, a pawn that is protected and not hanging. I now think the point of d4 is a cheap shot at a wing pawn. It isn't.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn gives the opponent more access to your king. A better move would have been moving your queen to e7 because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: I recaptured into Qxd8+. That's the whole story: queen trade with check, then Nxe5, because my c6-knight is pulled off the defense. I even recaptured with the knight and kept castling, so 'more access to your king' is the wrong frame. Qe7 'because you can likely take a pawn' is a lie — e5 is defended by the knight. Don't invent a free pawn when the lesson is 'don't walk into the queen trade.'

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the black c8-bishop and the black king and you skewer the black king, exposing the black f8-bishop.
flags.critique: This is a queen trade with check so you can take e5 next. I do not keep the c8-bishop. I do not keep the f8-bishop. Calling it a fork and a skewer is detector vomit. Teach the combination: check, they recapture, the e-pawn hangs.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your c6-knight is the strongest move because the queen was undefended.
flags.critique: I am recapturing the queen that just took my queen. That is not winning material and 'undefended' is a tautology for a check I have to answer. Mention that this knight just abandoned e5 — that's the punchline of White's last move.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Bd6 develops and hits the knight on e5. That knight sits there for the next ten plies while you beg White to play Nd3, and you never told me I was already attacking it. Empty 'strongest move' on the one developing move that actually creates the theme.

flags.quote: Moving your g8-knight to f6 is playable, but taking the knight on e5 with your d6-bishop would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Bxe5 does not pin a pawn to a rook. Bishops don't pin along a file. The real idea is take the octopus on e5 and wreck the pawn cover if they recapture. Inventing a pin makes me look at the f-file for a tactic that isn't there.

flags.quote: Castling kingside doesn't ease a difficult position because it gives your king shelter and brings your rook closer to the center. A better move would have been taking the knight on e5 with your d6-bishop because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: You used the good things about castling as the reason castling failed. That's a template crash, not a lesson. Then you say Bxe5 'keeps your king safer' as if taking a knight is prophylaxis. If the eval wants Bxe5, tell me the knight is the problem — don't argue with yourself in one sentence.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b3 is a mistake, but moving your e5-knight to d3 would be better.
flags.critique: Nd3 again, still no why. That knight has been sitting on e5 under fire since Bd6. If the lesson is 'your knight is unstable, tuck it in,' say that. 'Nd3 would be better' is a move name, not coaching.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e6 with your c4-bishop puts it where the black d8-knight and pawn can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your c4-bishop to e2.
flags.critique: Trading bishops is not the bug. Nxe6 adds a second attacker to e5 and the knight falls. You mashed the recapture and the hanging knight into one sentence that sounds like I hung the bishop I just captured with. Be2 is also a retreat with no idea attached.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e6 with your d8-knight is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Of course the piece that just captured is 'undefended' — I am recapturing. The reason this recapture is the one you wanted is that the knight on e6 now double-attacks e5. You already said I'd lose a knight if White took on e6. Connect it.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to b2 is playable, but moving your e5-knight to d3 would be better.
flags.critique: The e5 knight is now attacked twice. This is the hanging-piece ply and you whispered 'Nd3' with no reason. Scream that the knight falls. I am a 1200. I need the word hanging.

flags.quote: Moving your e5-knight to d7 is a blunder, but moving your e5-knight to d3 would be better.
flags.critique: 446 centipawns and you still won't tell me what I did. I jumped a knight onto d7 in their camp, where a rook can pin it down next move. Nd3 for the fifth time is not an explanation. If the piece is getting trapped or rounded up, say trapped.

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to d8 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I put a rook on the knight you just parked on d7. That is the entire move. Blank strongest-move copy on a hanging-piece attack is malpractice.

flags.quote: Moving your d7-knight to b6 is a blunder, but moving your d7-knight to e5 would be better.
flags.critique: b6 is the fork square. Next you'll tell me Bc5+ hits this knight and the king — so why didn't you say I ran onto the fork? Lichess called this an inaccuracy; you said blunder and still skipped the tactic.

flags.quote: Moving your e4-knight to d2 is a blunder, but moving your bishop to c5 would be better because you fork the white b6-knight and the white king and then take a knight.
flags.critique: The Bc5+ fork is the first time this game you named a real tactic clearly. Then you slapped 'blunder' on Nd2, which actually attacks a rook, while Lichess said inaccuracy. Don't bury a good fork lesson under a panic label for a move that is just worse, not suicidal.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-rook to e1 is the strongest move because it saves your e1-rook from capture.
flags.critique: There was no rook on e1. The knight on d2 was taking the rook on f1, and I moved that rook. You labeled the destination square as the piece being saved. I now think I have two rooks on the e-file in my head. Also you called a 135-centipawn swing 'best' and 'That's the one.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f4 with your bishop is a blunder because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: You told me it is a blunder because I took a free pawn. The pawn is not free — the knight on e2 recaptures and I drop a bishop, 679 centipawns, game almost thrown. 'Undefended' is factually false and the because-clause is inverted. The better move is the same Bc5+ fork you already mentioned. Lead with 'you hung the bishop,' not 'nice capture.'

flags.quote: Taking the rook on e8 with your e1-rook is the strongest move because you fork the black d8-rook and the black king and you take the defender of the black d8-rook.
flags.critique: I traded rooks with check. That is not a fork I get to keep, and 'you take the defender of the other rook' is a fancy way to say the two rooks were next to each other. Stop stacking tactic nouns on a recapture.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d7 is a blunder, but moving your rook to d1 would be better because your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: Rd1 is better because it hits the knight sitting on d2 in my camp, not because files are a lifestyle. I blundered 336 centipawns hopping a knight while two black knights and a rook are eating my second rank. 'Open file' is what you say when you don't want to look at the board.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your pawn to h3 lets black force checkmate in 4 moves. This lets black force checkmate in 4 moves. A better move would have been moving your bishop to c1 because you can likely take a knight.
flags.critique: You said mate in 4 twice in a row, then opened with 'you are still worse' like I'm down a pawn instead of getting mated. Bc1 'likely take a knight' is weasel copy for the hanging knight on d2 that is part of the mate. If you see mate, stop the eval-frame throat-clearing and name the mating pieces.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on g2 with your rook is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: This is check, in a mate-in-4 you just announced. I do not care that g2 was 'undefended' or that I 'take the defender of the white pawn' — which pawn? Teach the mating pattern: rook checks on g2, king is boxed. You had mate language one ply ago and then described a pawn grab.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h1 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: I am in check. h1 is the corner they are mating me in. 'Harder to attack' and 'That's the one' on a forced king move into mate is gaslighting. If it's the only legal square, say it's forced. Don't praise king safety while the eval is mate.

flags.quote: Moving your d2-knight to f3 is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your rook on the white pawn.
flags.critique: This is the mating net, not a discovered attack on some pawn. Knight to f3 covers g1 and h2 so the rook can finish it. I am a beginner staring at mate and you pointed at a pawn. Stop letting discovered-attack detectors outrank mate.

suggestions.title: Stop praising captures that are blunders
suggestions.detail: chooseConcept lets `capture` win CONCEPT_PRIORITY on any teachable capture, and explainPlayedAsBenefit then feeds pickBenefitReasons into the because-clause. Bxf4 (ply 36) became 'a blunder because the pawn was undefended.' Do not treat capture/check/development as benefit concepts when classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder; use problemReasons only. A 1200 who hung a bishop cannot hear that the capture was the good part.

suggestions.title: Prefer mate copy over capture soup
suggestions.detail: selectBecauseReasons keeps capture/wins_material/discovered_attack/removed_defender and drops forces_mate. Rxg2+ and Nf3 (plies 44, 46) are mating moves described as undefended pawns. Rank allows_mate/forces_mate first, and treat check as a first-class because-reason whenever evalAfter is mate. Also fix describeConsequence duplicating allows_mate: containsIgnoreCase(problem, consequence) misses 'this lets black force checkmate' vs 'lets black force checkmate' (ply 43).

suggestions.title: Never justify a bad move with its upside
suggestions.detail: When problemReasons is empty, becauseReasons falls back to playedBenefits. Castling (ply 20) then reads 'doesn't ease a difficult position because it gives your king shelter.' If the verdict is negative, omit playedBecause rather than attaching castle/king_safer/wins_material. Same bug as Kh1 'harder to attack' during mate (ply 45): king_safer must not fire on a forced move in a mating net.

suggestions.title: Drop tactics that die on recapture
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics already exists but only runs on suggestedBenefits. Apply it to played benefits. Qxd8+ (ply 11) and Rxe8+ (ply 39) are recaptured checks labeled fork+skewer+pin+removed_defender. d4 (ply 7) unveils Bc1 onto a safe h6 pawn. Require SEE or a surviving target; geometric detectors without net material or mate should not reach describeBecause.

suggestions.title: Don't call recaptures undefended wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material currently fires when capturedSeeCp >= 80, including equal recaptures (Nxd8, Nxe6, Rxe8). Copy then says 'the queen/bishop/rook was undefended.' Track whether the captured unit just arrived on that square last ply, or require a positive net after the recapture. Recaptures should say 'you have to take back' or name the follow-up (e5 now hangs, e5 is attacked twice), not 'you won material.'

suggestions.title: Name the square the piece fled from
suggestions.detail: retreatedToSafety builds saves_piece with square: effects.move.to, so Rfe1 'saves your e1-rook from capture' (ply 35). Use move.from (or the hanging square before the move). A 1200 will literally look for a rook that isn't there.

suggestions.title: Require a because-clause or drop strongest
suggestions.detail: Bc4, h6, Bd6, Rad8 and others render 'is the strongest move.' with reasons []. If no ranked benefit survives, fall back to a concrete effect (attacks f7, stops Ng5, attacks the e5-knight, attacks the d7-knight) or say 'a fine developing move' instead of strongest. Empty strongest plus 'That's the one.' is the default voice of this dump and it teaches nothing on the named Italian ideas.

suggestions.title: Don't recommend Nd3 with no threat named
suggestions.detail: Nd3 is the suggested move on plies 17, 23, 27, 29, 31, usually with suggestedBecause null. The actual story is the e5-knight hanging or under-supported. If suggestedBenefits is empty, pull the ignored_threat/hanging fact for that piece rather than emitting 'X would be better.' Same for Rd1 (ply 41): open_file lost to 'your rook attacks the knight on d2.' Repeated empty suggestions of the same SAN should reuse the hanging-piece reason, not a new shrug.

whatWorked: Nc6 (ply 4) actually said the e-pawn was hanging — rare opening copy with a real threat.
Kingside castling (ply 15) named king safety and the rook in one sentence and meant it.
Nxf4 as the improvement to Rfe8 (ply 28) correctly said you take the defender of the e5-knight.
Ne2 (ply 29) named the hanging e4-pawn and the attacker. That's the format I want on every blunder.
Bc5+ fork of king and b6-knight (plies 34 and 36 suggestions) is the clearest tactic sentence in the game.
Nxf4 recapture (ply 37) plus the discovered rook hit on e6 is a real combination, not detector soup.
Re2 (ply 42) teaching the seventh rank is concrete and true.
Mate-in-4 on h3 (ply 43) was detected — then immediately duplicated and buried under 'still worse.'
